resolved.meaning: A numeric gap is exact instance geometry. Rhythm is applied at the preset rungs, never at a consume site, so an instance that asked for 8px must still read 8px.

Rhythm scales the room around a control, never the control. Bound to control-bearing targets deliberately: a LAYOUT container's intrinsic height legitimately grows when its gaps grow, so checking this everywhere would report the intended effect as a violation. Includes the indirect vectors a rule could use to change the control's rendered size without touching height/block-size directly: max-height (the physical dual of max-block-size), aspect-ratio (a fixed width plus a moved aspect-ratio moves height too), scale, zoom and contain-intrinsic-size. The two `@rect-*` reserved observables are the RENDERED box read from getBoundingClientRect, so a padding/border/transform mutation that changes what is actually painted cannot hide behind an unmoved computed longhand.

The coarse-pointer touch floor must survive every rhythm stop by construction rather than by clamping, so the hit box of a bound interactive target may not move at all. 'May not move at all' includes the ceiling as well as the floor (max-inline-size and its physical dual max-width; min-width is min-inline-size's physical dual) and the indirect vectors that resize a box without changing its own size properties: aspect-ratio, scale, zoom and contain-intrinsic-size. The two `@rect-*` reserved observables are the RENDERED box read from getBoundingClientRect, so this assertion does not depend on width/height strings alone.

Icon boxes are sized by the icon channels, not by layout rhythm. Includes the indirect vectors that could change an icon's rendered box without moving its own width/height/inline-size/block-size: aspect-ratio, scale, zoom and contain-intrinsic-size. The two `@rect-*` reserved observables are the RENDERED box read from getBoundingClientRect, so this assertion does not depend on width/height strings alone.
Rhythm is a spacing axis. It shares no channel with the type scale, so no measured element may change a font metric under it.
Rhythm shares no channel with any palette seed.
Border geometry belongs to the shape axis. Radius is included on purpose: a rhythm stop that moved a corner would be reaching a channel it does not own.
A numeric gap is exact instance geometry. Rhythm is applied at the preset rungs, never at a consume site, so an instance that asked for 8px must still read 8px.

resolved.meaning: The Grid family narrows the control-level claim onto its own root.
partiallyMechanised: track templates: getComputedStyle resolves grid-template-columns/rows to USED track sizes rather than the authored template, and flexible tracks in a fixed-width container must absorb any gap change by arithmetic (measured repeat(2, minmax(0,1fr)) at 1280px: 632.5px tracks + 15px gap at normal, 631px tracks + 18px gap at airy, both exactly 1280). Asserting did-not-move on them reports the control's intended effect as a violation, for the same reason control height is not asserted on a layout container.

scopeOfRun.note: A fixture that names a real component takes its element shape FROM THAT COMPONENT — rendered, then pasted — never from the CSS. Deriving the shape from the CSS is what let `button-modern-md` and `input-modern-md` sit on `.ds-btn`/`.ds-input` for months: a selector states what an element must carry to be MATCHED, and says nothing about whether any component emits it, so a CSS-derived fixture can measure a rule that never paints and still look green. Regenerate a component shape by rendering the engine implementation with `renderToStaticMarkup` and pasting the result, minus React-generated ids, plus `data-probe`. The synthetic fixtures (the two skeleton controls and the token readout) are exempt: they exist to read a dial, not to stand for a component. `requiresSelectors` is not documentation either: the harness asserts each string occurs verbatim in the CSS it is about to measure and marks the fixture `unmatched` if it does not, so a fixture that stops being matched is reported, never silently measured as zero. Pin selectors and the paint statement, never a declaration's VALUE — a precedence ruling would then read as a broken fixture.
